blocks.customer-response: Write a clear external response with confirmed facts, user impact, workaround, and next update. Do not expose internal-only evidence or uncertain root causes.
blocks.data-analysis: Define the population, clean the dataset, state missing coverage, compute metrics, and separate observation from inference. Do not treat estimates as measured values.
blocks.documentation-editing: Preserve factual meaning, reduce unclear language, validate examples, and keep links working. Do not invent benchmark results or product support.
blocks.incident-triage: Build a timestamped evidence chain across application, infrastructure, database, and provider signals. Prefer containment and reversible action over speculative code changes.
blocks.migration-planning: Classify changes into mechanical transforms, semantic rewrites, compatibility checks, and rollout batches. Do not merge changes or publish releases.
blocks.pull-request-review: Review changed code for correctness, tests, compatibility, and maintainability. Do not modify version numbers or publish packages during review.
blocks.release-control: Calculate package versions, dependency propagation, changelog sections, and publish order. Do not approve code quality or edit implementation files.
blocks.security-assessment: Inspect trust boundaries, authentication, session handling, secrets, and data exposure. Treat missing evidence as unknown and do not claim an exploit.

core: Use supplied evidence. Mark unknowns. Keep changes reversible. Run the same acceptance checks before and after any architecture change.
